title: Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga: Temple Guide, Route from Pune and Best Time
seoTitle: Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga: Temple, Route & Best Time | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Visit Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga in the Sahyadri hills: the temple, darshan tips, the road from Pune and Mumbai, forest treks and the best time to go.
description: A visitor's guide to Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga in Pune district: the temple and the source of the Bhima river, darshan practicalities, the road from Pune and Mumbai, trekking routes from Khandas, Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary and its giant squirrels, seasons, stays and the other site that claims the name.
dek: Bhimashankar is a Jyotirlinga in the forest: a stone temple high in the Sahyadri hills, where the Bhima river begins.

hero.alt: The stone shikhara of Bhimashankar Temple in the Sahyadri hills, Pune district

intro: Bhimashankar Temple stands at about 1,000 m in the Sahyadri (Western Ghats), in Khed taluka of Pune district, about 110 km from Pune. Tradition places the source of the Bhima river here. The temple's older stone core was extended in the 18th century, when the Maratha minister Nana Phadnavis is credited with building the hall and shikhara.

The temple lies inside Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary, known for the Indian giant squirrel (shekru), Maharashtra's state animal. In the monsoon the hills are wrapped in cloud and waterfalls, which draws trekkers as well as pilgrims.
quickAnswer: Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga is about 110 km (three and a half to four hours) from Pune by road, via Rajgurunagar and Manchar, with a winding final climb. From Mumbai it is about 210 km by road, or trekkers walk up from Khandas near Karjat. Darshan is busiest on Mondays, in Shravan and on Maha Shivratri. September to February is the best time; the monsoon is beautiful but wet.
takeaways: Bhimashankar is about 110 km from Pune and about 210 km from Mumbai by road.
It lies inside Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary, home of the Indian giant squirrel.
Trekkers climb from Khandas (Karjat side) by the Ganesh Ghat or the steeper Shidi Ghat route.
Avoid driving the ghat road at night.
Assam's government has promoted a site in Kamrup as Bhimashankar; the Pune temple is the one most pilgrims visit.

sections.heading: The temple
paras: The temple is built of dark stone in the Nagara style, set in a hollow below the car park and reached by a flight of steps. Inside the sanctum is the linga, reached through a pillared hall. Nearby shrines include Kamalaja Devi and the spring associated with the Bhima's source.

sections.heading: Darshan tips
list: There are steps down to the temple and back up; allow extra time for older visitors.
Weekday mornings are quieter; Mondays, Shravan and Maha Shivratri see very long queues.
Keep phones and bags minimal; follow the notices on photography.
Carry cash for small purchases; the hilltop has limited facilities.

items.name: Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary
body: Evergreen forest protecting the Indian giant squirrel, with birds and butterflies. Walks start near the temple.

items.name: Treks from Khandas
body: The Ganesh Ghat route is longer and gentler; the Shidi Ghat route uses steep steps and ladders and is risky in heavy rain. Both are popular monsoon treks; go with an experienced group.

items.name: Viewpoints
body: Nagphani point and Gupt Bhimashankar are short walks from the temple, with views over the Konkan when clear.

sections.heading: Another claim to the name
paras: Most pilgrims and the traditional lists identify the sixth Jyotirlinga with this temple near Pune. The Assam government has also promoted a Shiva temple in Kamrup as Bhimashankar, citing a reference to Dakini hills in the Shiva Purana. We mention it because readers ask; this guide does not settle the question.

sections.heading: How to reach and where to stay
list: From Pune: about 110 km via Rajgurunagar (Khed), Manchar and Ghodegaon; state transport buses run from Pune.
From Mumbai: about 210 km by road via Pune or the Khed route; trekkers take a train to Karjat and a local vehicle to Khandas.
Stay: basic lodges and MTDC-style stays near the temple, or stay in Pune or Manchar and make a day trip.
The final ghat stretch is steep and winding; drive in daylight.

rows: Leave Pune to avoid traffic at Rajgurunagar
Walk to Gupt Bhimashankar or Nagphani point
Lunch at the hilltop stalls; start back by 3 pm to finish the ghat in daylight

safety: Darshan waits vary from minutes to many hours; no one can guarantee quick darshan, so plan buffer time.
Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) and follow the temple's rules on phones, bags and photography.
In the monsoon, check trail conditions and avoid the Shidi Ghat route in heavy rain.
Drive the ghat road in daylight and watch for fog.
packing: Rain jacket and good-grip shoes in the monsoon

faqs.q: How far is Bhimashankar from Pune?
faqs.a: About 110 km, or three and a half to four hours by road.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Bhimashankar?
faqs.a: September to February. The monsoon is scenic but wet and slippery.

faqs.q: Is Bhimashankar in a wildlife sanctuary?
faqs.a: Yes, Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary, known for the Indian giant squirrel.

faqs.q: Where can I stay at Bhimashankar?
faqs.a: There are simple lodges near the temple; most visitors stay in Pune or Manchar and make a day trip.
